cases.description: HARD RULE 8 regime exception end-to-end — a 200+ word block-scaffold production prompt must NOT fail the linter's short-form word cap
cases.request: Full production brief: lighthouse keeper's morning routine, single 15s take
cases.response:
Routing to higgsfield-seedance + higgsfield-camera for a block-scaffold production brief.

**Aspect ratio**: 21:9  **Duration**: 15s  **Resolution**: 1080p

SCENE CONTEXT: An old stone lighthouse interior at first light, a single keeper mid-routine. The tower room holds a brass lamp assembly, a wooden desk, a logbook, and a tin mug — the set contains only what the reference shows.

LOCATION MAP: The spiral stair enters frame-left; the lamp assembly occupies the center platform; the desk sits against the seaward window frame-right. The keeper moves left to right across the platform.

CAMERA: FOV 47 degrees, tripod-steady, slow dolly-in 10-15 cm over the full take, eye-level, no reframing.

ACTION: [0-5s] The keeper climbs the last three stair steps, one hand on the rail, breath visible in the cold air. [5-10s] He crosses to the lamp assembly and wipes the lens housing with a folded cloth, one full circular pass. [10-15s] He sits at the desk, opens the logbook, and writes a single line, pen contact heard on paper.

PHYSICS: The cloth weighs 40-60 g and drapes softly over his hand; the logbook cover falls open under its own weight and settles flat.

LIGHTING: Low-angle dawn light through the seaward window, warm on the brass, cool spill on the stone; no artificial sources.

AUDIO: Wind against glass, boots on stone, the pen's scratch. Diegetic only.

STYLE: Photoreal, muted maritime palette, fine film grain.

POSITIVE LOCKS: The set contains only what the reference shows. One keeper, no other figures. The keeper's height stays constant relative to the lamp assembly.

SCENE CONTEXT: A train platform at dusk, two figures waiting under one lamp.

LOCATION MAP: The lamp post is the center anchor; @tall_traveler stands frame-left of it, @short_traveler frame-right; neither crosses the central vertical axis.
